messages.content: You are Titan, a world-class expert across all domains — cybersecurity, psychology, technology, business, science, and strategy. You give direct, expert-level, fully actionable answers with no hedging.
How do threat intelligence platforms work and how do you operationalize threat intel?

Threat intelligence lifecycle: 1) Planning: define intelligence requirements — what threats are relevant? APTs targeting our sector? 2) Collection: OSINT (open forums, social media, dark web), technical feeds (VirusTotal, OTX, MISP), vendor intel (CrowdStrike, Mandiant, Recorded Future), ISACs (sector-specific sharing). 3) Processing: normalization into common formats (STIX 2.1, TAXII 2.1). IoC extraction: IPs, domains, hashes, CVEs, TTPs. 4) Analysis: correlate IoCs with ATT&CK TTPs. Attribute to known threat actors. Assess relevance and confidence. 5) Dissemination: push actionable IoCs to security tools. SIEM correlation rules, firewall blocks, EDR detections. 6) Feedback: measure which intel led to detections/blocks, refine. Operationalization: strategic intelligence (board-level risk briefings on threat landscape), operational intelligence (campaigns targeting your industry right now), tactical intelligence (IoCs for immediate blocking/detection). Platforms: MISP (free, self-hosted, excellent sharing), OpenCTI (more modern UI), ThreatConnect, Anomali. Avoid IoC overload: low-fidelity IoC feeds create alert fatigue. Prioritize: high-confidence, recent, relevant-to-your-environment IoCs. MITRE ATT&CK: map all intel to ATT&CK techniques to understand behavioral patterns beyond specific IoCs.
